resources.string: Grayscale on every screen wake. One tile, one tap at a time.
Secure-settings permission is missing. Run the ADB command below, then tap Retry / resume.
Android could not apply grayscale. Check the permission, then tap Retry / resume. See logcat tag GrayWake for details.
Android blocked monitoring from starting. Open Gray Wake and tap Retry / resume. Check background battery restrictions if this repeats.
Quiet status while grayscale automation or a snooze is active.
Reapplies grayscale whenever the screen wakes.
Color is on. Grayscale resumes automatically.
Install the app, enable USB debugging on your phone, connect it to a computer with ADB, and run:
adb shell pm grant dev.graywake android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
Open Quick Settings, tap Edit, and drag Grayscale into your active tiles.
The tile was not added. Use Quick Settings → Edit to add it manually.
That settings page is unavailable on this device.
Disabled → Enabled → Snooze until next wake → 5 min → 15 min → 30 min → 45 min → 60 min → 12 h → Disabled

Enabled turns grayscale on now and on each wake. Snooze until next wake turns color on until the screen next turns on, then returns to Enabled. Tap again before that wake to select Snooze 5 min. Timed snoozes start a fresh duration on each tap and return to Enabled at expiry. If the phone is asleep, grayscale resumes on its next wake without waking it just for the timer.

This changes Android color correction. Snooze and Disable turn correction off; a previous correction mode is not restored. Other grayscale features, such as Bedtime mode, can still affect the screen.

A quiet foreground service runs while enabled or snoozing. Notification permission is optional. Disable before uninstalling, clearing data, or force-stopping the app; those actions do not undo a system color setting.

If Android stops monitoring, reopen this page and tap Retry / resume, or tap the paused tile. Some phones also need unrestricted battery usage for reliable background operation.
